title: The First Hybrid Car Was Built in 1900 ⚙️🕰️ #shorts

scenes.text: The first working hybrid car was built in nineteen hundred, with its motors inside the wheels.
That year in Paris, a young Ferdinand Porsche showed an electric car with a motor in each front wheel hub.
No gearbox, no chains, no driveshaft. Each motor made about two and a half horsepower.
The catch? Batteries weighing up to eighteen hundred kilos, for about twenty-five miles of range.
So he added gasoline engines that never drove the wheels. They spun generators instead. A series hybrid: Semper Vivus, always alive.
With the engines running, it could go about a hundred miles.
Hub motors later drove NASA's moon rovers. So why don't most EVs use them? Follow EV Drive.
